chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran or another, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to him: A man made a bequest to another man of one-third or one-quarter of his wealth, then the man (the testator) was killed by mistake. He meant the testator. He said: 'This bequest is paid from his inheritance and from his blood-money (diyah).'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a man's bequest if he is killed accidentally before distributing his wealth?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that an accidental death (qatl khata') does not invalidate the testator's bequest, distinguishing it from intentional homicide which may affect inheritance rights. The ruling ensures the beneficiary receives their share from both the primary estate and the compensation (diyah) paid by the killer, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the debt of the bequest is settled from all available assets. This highlights the principle that the testator's obligation persists regardless of the manner of death, provided the estate is sufficient.
